correctness.rationale: Every proper independent Kneser color class is a star or triangle. A size-r star has a common-neighbor witness exactly for r<=n-3; a triangle always has one for n>=5. Capacity rules out n-2 colors for n=5,6,7, and explicit complete partitions provide n-1. For n>=8, the canonical known optimum proper-coloring classification converts the CD condition into tournament maximum outdegree <=n-6; balanced tournaments exist for all n>=8, so n-2 works. Unique triangle/center assignments prove the bijection. Direct graph-witness verification of all constructions n=5..100 and exhaustive tournament cases n=8,9 independently corroborate the proof. Finite checks alone are not used as the infinite argument.

value.rationale: Answers a specifically documented 2024 mathematical open problem on a canonical infinite Kneser graph family. The abrupt n=8 threshold where CD chromatic equals ordinary chromatic is structural, not a renamed standard scalar. The bijection with bounded-score tournaments classifies every optimum and supplies natural nontrivial counts 1344 and 435456.
